gloss: the art of the staff (a Japanese martial art)

definitions.gloss: bōjutsu; the martial art of fighting with a staff
definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese martial art that uses a wooden staff, typically around 180 cm long (the {六|ろく}{尺|しゃく}{棒|ぼう}, 'six-foot staff'), as its principal weapon. Techniques include strikes, thrusts, sweeps, and blocks, and {棒術|ぼうじゅつ} is one component of classical weapons training ({古武道|こぶどう}), often taught alongside or within schools of {柔術|じゅうじゅつ} or {剣術|けんじゅつ}. Also refers to the broader category of staff-based martial techniques.

examples.japanese: {棒術|ぼうじゅつ}を{習|なら}う。
{祖父|そふ}は{若|わか}いころ{棒術|ぼうじゅつ}の{道場|どうじょう}に{通|かよ}っていた。
examples.english: My grandfather attended a bōjutsu dojo when he was young.

examples.japanese: {沖縄|おきなわ}には{古|ふる}くから{独自|どくじ}の{棒術|ぼうじゅつ}の{流派|りゅうは}が{伝|つた}わっている。
examples.english: A unique school of bōjutsu has been passed down in Okinawa since ancient times.

examples.japanese: {演武会|えんぶかい}では、{剣術|けんじゅつ}や{柔術|じゅうじゅつ}だけでなく{棒術|ぼうじゅつ}の{型|かた}も{披露|ひろう}された。
examples.english: At the demonstration, not only swordsmanship and jūjutsu but also bōjutsu forms were performed.

notes:
Compound of {棒|ぼう} ('stick; staff; rod') and {術|じゅつ} ('technique; art'). The {〜術|じゅつ} suffix names many martial and practical arts: {剣術|けんじゅつ} ('swordsmanship'), {柔術|じゅうじゅつ} ('jūjutsu'), {忍術|にんじゅつ} ('ninjutsu'), {弓術|きゅうじゅつ} ('archery'), {馬術|ばじゅつ} ('horseback riding'), {手術|しゅじゅつ} ('surgery').

USAGE:
- Treated as a noun; verbs include {棒術|ぼうじゅつ}を{習|なら}う ('learn'), を{練習|れんしゅう}する ('practice'), の{稽古|けいこ}をする ('train in').
- Does not take する directly.
- Often specified by region or school: {沖縄|おきなわ}{棒術|ぼうじゅつ} ('Okinawan bōjutsu'), {神道|しんとう}{夢想|むそう}{流|りゅう}{棒術|ぼうじゅつ} ('Shintō Musō-ryū bōjutsu').

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {棒術|ぼうじゅつ}を{習|なら}う: to learn bōjutsu
- {棒術|ぼうじゅつ}の{稽古|けいこ}: bōjutsu practice / training
- {棒術|ぼうじゅつ}の{型|かた}: bōjutsu forms / kata
- {棒術|ぼうじゅつ}の{流派|りゅうは}: school / tradition of bōjutsu
- {棒術|ぼうじゅつ}の{演武|えんぶ}: bōjutsu demonstration
- {沖縄|おきなわ}{棒術|ぼうじゅつ}: Okinawan bōjutsu

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {杖術|じょうじゅつ}: jōjutsu — art of the shorter {杖|じょう} (around 128 cm); related but distinct weapon.
- {剣術|けんじゅつ}: swordsmanship — classical sword arts.
- {槍術|そうじゅつ}: spearmanship — uses a spear ({槍|やり}), not a staff.
- {薙刀術|なぎなたじゅつ}: naginata arts — glaive-style pole weapon.
- {古武道|こぶどう}: classical Japanese martial arts — the broader category that includes {棒術|ぼうじゅつ}.

CULTURAL CONTEXT:
{棒術|ぼうじゅつ} developed in feudal Japan as both a battlefield skill and a self-defense art for travelers, monks, and commoners who were not permitted to carry swords. Okinawan {古武道|こぶどう}, influenced by Chinese weapon traditions, preserves a particularly rich repertoire of staff techniques that complement karate training.
